newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Stockpile bid concerns Australia wool authority.
newsitem.headline: Stockpile bid concerns Australia wool authority.

text.p: Reports of a proposal by a private group to buy Australia's wool stockpile raised concerns about maximising the value for woolgrowers and about market confidence, Wool International chief executive officer Bob Richardson said on Monday.

Richardson was responding to a A$1.2 billion offer by former oil company executive David Sasson to buy the remaining 1.8 million bale stockpile and to buy woolgrowers' equity entitlements in Wool International.
He said Wool International had not received any new proposal from Sasson since its rejection of a similar proposal nine months ago, but added that any new proposal would be considered on its merits.
But Wool International's competitive strategy was to offer greasy wool to a wide range of customers, he said.
"A single deal with one customer would be inconsistent with this competitive strategy. It may maximise stockpile profits to one company at the expense of woolgrowers," he said.
Claims that the Sasson purchase would save A$30 million in storage and handling by shipping wool overseas were unsubstantiated.
WI's total costs for storage and handling for this season would be less than A$17 million, he said.
WI's experience was that shipping and processing could only be justified in limited circumstances where higher net returns offset the additional cost, he said.
